question.problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$N=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \sqrt{6} & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & \sqrt{5} & 2 \\ \sqrt{3} & 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the $1$st row contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(N) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \sqrt{6} & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & \sqrt{5} & 2 \\ \sqrt{3} & 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{5} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{5} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{5} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot ((-1)\cdot \sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{5})=-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
det(N)=-10.
$$
